IS t 9607 - 1980 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
TERTIARY LEVEL 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 30 September 1980, after the draft finalized by the Optical and 
Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 Tertiary level is a medium-accuracy level used for third and fourth 
order levelling operations. These operations include level control and 
alignment in construction, irrigation, pipe laying and drainage ditches and 
determining profiles, contours, etc. 

0.3 Tertiary level ( see Fig. 1 ) mainly consists of an internal focussing 
telescope having compaiatively low magnification. It is light in weight 
and quite sturdy in design. The circular and cylindrical bubbles are seen 
in a mirror fitted over them to facilitate the observations. Its design is 
quite simple as compared to a primary or secondary level. This may be 
either of automatic type or of non-automatic type; the latter containing 
no compensator. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the requirements of non-automatic type tertiary 
level capable of attaining standard deviation of ± 5 mm in 1 km of double 
levelling. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose, of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 1399- 
1959* shall apply. 

3. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

3.0 The tertiary level shall conform to the requirements laid down in 
IS : 988-1959f and to the requirements laid down in 3 of IS : 2754-1964}. 

•Glossary of terms used in optical technology. 
fOeneral requirements for optical components. 
JGcneral requirements for optical instruments. 



18 1 9607- 1980 




5 

W 

> 

< 

M 

H 
05 



Ex 



IS I 9607- 1980 

3.1 The base plate of the instrument shall have provision for fitting the 
level on the stand. It shall have a central hole of such dimension that a 
clamping screw of size M16 x 2 may be fitted well into it. 

3.2 A pressure plate shall be provided to keep the foot screws firm in the 
sleeves of the base plate. 

3.3 The level shall be provided with a cylindrical axis and bushing made 
of special high grade alloy steel which cnsuies reliable operation at any 
temperature without special attention to oiling, cleaning, adjustment, etc. 

3.4 The instrument shall be compact, solid and highly stable. The 
telescope body and level casing shall be tooled from one piece. 

3.5 All optical parts shall be provided with antirefiection coatings. 

3.6 Bubbles 

3.6.1 The bubbles provided with the level shall conform to the require- 
ments of IS: 1632-1960*. 

3.6.2 The instrument shall be provided with a circular bubble for quick 
levelling in the beginning. It shall be fitted with a plane circular reflector 
( mirror ) for ease of observations of the air bell. The bubble shall be 
provided with capstan or square head screws for adjustment. This type 
of screw shall be adopted to enable the use of tomy pin/spanner during 
adjustment and thus avoiding undue pressure on bubble. 

3.6.3 The level shall be fitted with a medium sensitivity cylindrical 
bubble having provision of a plane mirror. The plane mirror shall be 
fitted over the bubble in such a way that it can easily be retained in any 
position and shall not fall due to its own weight. The cylindrical bubble 
shall be capable of adjustment by means of capstan or square head screw 
both side-ways and in the vertical plane. 

3.7 Horizontal Circle — If agreed to between supplier and purchaser, 
the level shall be provided with a horizontal metallic circle. The circle 
shall be graduated in 360 degrees; the marking being made at each degree 
and figuring after each ten degrees. The graduations shall be such that 
it shall be possible to estimate one tenth of a degree. 

3.8 Telescope 

3.8.1 The telescope shall be provided with an internal focussing 
arrangement and its optics shall be provided with antirefiection coating 
conforming to IS : 8248-i976f. 



♦Specification for bubbles 

fSpecification for antirefiection coating on glass optical components. 



IS i 9607 - 1980 

3.8.2 The graticule of the telescope shall be provided with cross and 
stadia lines, the latter being provided in the vertical cross line. The 
distances of stadia lines from the horizontal cross line shall be equal. The 
gradicule lines shall be made on optically flat glass plate. Provision shall 
be made to move the gradicule plate precisely for adjusting collimation 
easily. 

3.8.3 The telescope shall be provided with a clamping screw, a screw 
for slow motion in the horizontal plane and a tilting screw for slow motion 
( tilting ) in the vertical plane. The head of the tilting screw shall be 
graduated and figured suitably to facilitate at the time of adjustment of 
bubbles as given in 5.2.1.1. 

3.8.4 A sighting arrangement shall be provided on the telescope for 
quick location of staff. 

3.9 Technical Data — The tertiary level shall conform to the following 
technical requirements: 

a) Magnification 20 to 25 x 

b) Clear aperture of objective 25 to 30 mm 

c) Field of view About 2 degrees 

d) Addition constant Practically 

e) Multiplication ( stadia ) constant 100 

f ) Shortest sighting distance About 1*5 metres 

g) Largest aiming distance for mm 80 m 
evaluation 

h) Sensitivity of circular bubble 10 minutes per 2 mm 

j ) Sensitivity of cylindrical bubble 60 seconds per 2 mm 

k) Accuracy of levelling the line of sight ± 12 seconds 

m) Levelling accuracy attainable, that is, ± 5 mm 

standard deviation ( mean square 
error) in 1 km of double levelling 

n) Horizontal circle graduations ( see 3.7 ) 

3.10 Case — The instrument shall be provided with a light metallic or 
well seasoned wooden case fitted with receptacles to hold the instrument 
and accessories. The case shall have suitable locking arrangements. A 
carrying handle or belt shall be provided with the case. 

3.11 Accessories — The following accessories shall be supplied with each 
instrument: 

a) Camel hair brush 1 

b) Tomy pin/spanner 2 



IS 1 9607 -1980 

c) Chamois leather 1 piece 

d) Screw driver 1 

e) Silica gel ( activated ) 1 packet 

f ) Tripod with clamping screw and plumb bob 1 

4. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 The movement of the clamping, slow motion and tilting screws and 
the motion of the different parts of the instrument shall be easy and 
smooth without undue stiffness, looseness or backlash. 

4.2 The clamping screw shall be such that it does not exert any strain on 
the clamped part. 

4.3 The motion of foot screws shall be smooth and these shall be 
protected from dust. 

4.4 The rotation of the telescope on its vertical axis shall be strainfree 
and smooth. 

4.5 The cylindrical bubble shall be capable of adjustment in horizontal 
as well as in vertical plane. 

4.6 The capstan screws provided for adjustment of different parts shall be 
such as not to exert any undue pressure on the respective parts. 

5. TESTS 

5.1 General Requirements Tests 

5.1.1 External — The level shall be initially checked for the following 
external defects: 

a) Loose, missing or damaged screws, nuts and other small parts; 
and 

b) Damage to telescope, bubble, engraving, external finish, etc. 

5.1.2 Internal — The instrument shall be checked for the following 
internal defects: 

a) Scratched, chipped or dirty optics; 

b) Damage to optical parts, graticule; deterioration of optical 
cement and anti-reflection coatings; 

c) Filming or fungus growth on optical surfaces; and 

d) Cloudiness or milky appearance on lenses and lack of clarity of 
graticule lines. 

5.1.3 The level shall be checked for smooth and adequate movement 
of the different parts. 



IS i 9607 - 1980 

5.1.4 Mechanical 

5.1.4,1 Clear aperture — The clear aperture of the objective shall be 
measured by a slide gauge or any suitable device. The measured value 
shall conform to the specified value. 

5*1.4.2 Bubbles — The sensitivity, consistency and all other para- 
meters of the bubbles shall be tested in accordance with 6.1 to 6.7 of 
IS : 1632*1960* and the values so obtained shall conform to the specified 
values within the tolerances laid down in Table II of IS : 1632-1960*. 

5.1.5 Optical 

5.1.5.1 Graticule alignment — The alignment of the graticule shall be 
tested with the help of a collimator and any misalignment shall be 
corrected by seeing the collimator's graticule. 

5.1.5.2 Definition — The definition of the telescope shall be tested 
with the help of a definition board given in Appendix E of IS : 2754-1964f. 
The circles, lines and squares of the board shall appear sharply defined 
without any distortion and colour over atleast two-thirds of the field of 
view. The definition and freedom from colour and distortion over the 
remaining field shall also be reasonably satisfactory. 

5.1.5.3 Magnification — The magnification of the telescope shall be 
tested by the method specified in Appendix C of IS : 2754-1964t. The 
measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent from the specified 
value. 

5.1.5.4 Resolving power — The resolving power of the telescope shall 
be measured by the method specified in Appendix F of IS : 2754-1964f. 
The measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent from the 
theoretical value. 

5.1.5.5 Field of view — The field of view of the telescope shall be 
tested by the method specified in Appendix D of IS : 2754-l964f. The 
measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent of the specified 
value. 

5.1.5.6 Parallax — The level shall be tested for parallax with the 
help of a collimator. After levelling the instrument with the help of two 
bubbles, the telescope shall be focussed on the collimator's graticule. 
There shall not be any apparent movement between the image of the 
collimator's graticule and the telescope's graticule on viewing the former 
through the eyepiece and moving eye at right angles to the axis of 
eyepiece. 



* Specification for bubbles. 

fGeneral requirements for optical instruments. 



IS t9607-1980 

5.1.5.7 Collimation — The collimation shall be tested in the labora- 
tory with the help of a collimator. The instrument shall be accurately 
levelled with the help of the two bubbles* provided and the collimator's 
graticule shall be focussed by it. Any deviation in the coincidence of 
image of the collimator's graticule and telescope graticule shall represent 
collimation error. This shall be corrected by moving the graticule with 
the help of adjusting screws provided in its mount. 

5.1.5.8 Strain — The optics of the tolescope shall be free from strain. 
It shall be tested as under: 

The level shall be so held that its telescope is in the path of light 
between two crossed nicols in a sensitive polariscope or strain viewer. 
The strain present in the telescope shall be revealed by the colour 
of the transmitted light. Before introducing the telescope of the level, 
the nicols shall be set for magenta colour. The strained areas in the 
optics of the telescope shall not show colour beyond indigo in the 
optical spectrum. 

5.2 Operational Tests 

5.2.1 General 

5.2.1.1 Bubbles — The instrument shall be placed on a perfectly flat 
and firm surface. The telescope shall be put parallel to any two foot 
screws facing the observer and the instrument shall be levelled by these 
two foot screws using the cylindrical bubble only. This shall be called the 
first position. The telescope shall then be rotated through 90° from this 
position in the clockwise direction and levelled with the help of the third 
screw only. This shall be called the second position. The telescope shall 
then be rotated through 90° from the second position in clockwise direc- 
tion so that it becomes again parallel to the first two foot screws as in the 
beginning ( first position ). The instrument shall then be levelled half by 
using two foot screws and half by using the tilting screw of the telescope. 
This process shall be repeated ( that is to level in the first position half by 
two foot screws parallel to telescope and half by tilting screw while in the 
second position by the third foot screw only ) till the cylindrical bubble is 
perfectly levelled in all the position of the telescope. 

The circular bubble shall then be brought in centre with the help of 
its adjusting screw without using foot screws and tilting screw till it remains 
in centre in all the positions of the instrument. 



♦The bubbles shall be first adjusted as given in 5.2.1.1. 

9 



IS s 9607 - 1980 

5.2.1.2 Reading accuracies 

a) The instrument shall be focussed on an appropriate vertical staff 
and the readings with the three graticule lines shall be taken. 
The mean of the three readings shall agree with the middle line 
readings within l'O mm. 

b) The height difference between two staff points shall be deter- 
mined by the level in its two different set ups on the same station. 
The two values shall agree within 3-0 mm. 

5.2.2 Field Test of Collimalion — The collimation shall be tested in the 
field by making observations on appropriate staves at equal and unequal 
distances. The two staves shall be placed 80 m apart and the instrument 
shall be placed in the middle of the line, that is at 40 m from each staff. 
The difference in heights of the two staff points, say X shall be determined 
in this situation. The instrument shall then be shifted to another point in 
the line such that the distance of one staff is 20 m while that of the other 
staff is 60 m from the instrument; retaining the staves precisely on their 
original points. The difference in heights, say T 9 of the two staff points 
shall again be determined in this situation. In case there is no collimation 
error, the height difference as determined in both the positions of the 
instrument shall remain the same within a tolerance of 2*0 mm. Beyond 
this limit, the collimation error shall be corrected as follows: 

For this, the instrument ( at this position of unequal staff distances ) 
shall be focussed on the farther staff, say B, and the horizontal wire 
is made to intersect the farther staff B, at original readings 
+ (T— X) x£ by means of tilting screw. This will disturb the bubble 
which should be brought to the centre of its run by means of capstan 
or square head screws at the end of the bubble tube. 

5.2.3 Field Test for Determination of Standard Deviation — Thel standard 
deviation ( error ) of the level shall be determined by the test method 
given in Appendix A. 

5*3 Climatic and Environmental Tests 

5.3.0 The following tests shall be carried on as given in IS : 2352-1963*. 
These are only type approval tests to be carried on sample basis as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. These are not to be used 
in routine testing during bulk production. 

5.3.1 Temperature Test — The level shall be subjected to cold and 
dry-heat test on severities — 10°C and 55°C respectively and checked 
thereafter for collimation, parallax, deterioration of cementing and 
antireflection coating. 



•Procedure for basic climatic and durability tests for optical instruments. 

10 



IS : 9607 - 1960 

5.3.2 Rain Test — The level, in its case, shall be tested in a 
rain chamber and after the test the level shall be checked lor ingress 
of moisture or water drops and for deterioration to any part of the 
instrument. 

5.3.3 Fungus ( Mould ) Growth Test — The level shall be tested for the 
fungus growth and checked thoroughly after the test. 

5.3.4 Vibration Test — The level, in its case, shall be clamped on to 
a vibration table giving approximately 450 vibrations per minute with 
an amplitude of 3 mm for a period of 5 minutes. After the test, the 
instrument shall be in perfect adjustment. 

6. MARKING 

6.1 The level shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark and the year of manufacture. 

6.1.1 The level may also be marked with the 1ST Certification Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the 
requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised bv ISI and operated by the 
producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence 
for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. PACKING 

7.1 The level shall be placed in its case together with its accessories 
and also an instruction booklet containing the guidelines for its use and 
adjustment. The case shall be suitably packed for transit. 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 5.2.3 ) 

METHOD OF TESTING STANDARD DEVIATION 
( ERROR ) OF LEVEL 

A-I. PROCEDURE 

A-l.l In order to test for standard deviation, the following requirements 
shall be fulfilled: 

a) Instrument concerned in good adjustment, 

b) Good staves and experienced stafTmen, 

11 



tS : 9*07 - I960 

c) Good and experienced observers, 

d) Four test lines ( legs ) connecting at least four and maximum 
five benchmarks, established by levelling of high precision. The 
length of each leg shall be 250 metres so that the total length of 
levelling line may be 1 km. The bench marks shall be selected 
in such a way that the four differential heights may be between 
0*5m to 2*5 m. 

A-1.2 The four test legs ( / a , / b , / c and / d ) shall be used in either of the 
following patterns (p), (q) or (r) ( see Fig. 2 ). 




(p; 

B 1f B2, B 2f B 4| B 5 




BM 1( BM2, BM3, BM 4 , 



B u B*> B 3 , B h 5 5 , B\. B\ y J3' 8 , B\, B' 5 , BM U B 2 M, BM 3 and BM i 
denote the bench marks. It may be seen that patterns (p) and (q) shall 
involve five bench marks u hile (r) shall involve only four bench marks. 

A-1.3 On each test leg five fore and five back le veilings shall be carried 
on so that 10 differential heights may be observed. The mean of these 
measurements shall be calculated and deviations of each value from the 
mean found out. The squares of deviations shall be taken and sum of such 
10 squares of deviations shall be found out in case of each leg. These 
shall be denoted as 2i'«/ a , 2i/*/ b , 2p 2 / and Sr/ 2 / d . If 2» a is denoted as the 
sum of the squares of deviations on four legs, then 2v* « 2y«/ a -f 2i;2/ b + 
IvH Q + Zv*l d .

The standard deviation shall be calculated by the formula: 
S per km of double levelling = ± k/ J^ 

A-2. PRECAUTIONS 

A-2.1 While carrying out the above test the following precautions shall be 
observed: 

a) The discordance between the fore and back values shall be kept 
within the specified tolerance for that particular type of level. 

b) All usual precautions and errors shall be strictly taken into 
consideration.
